suggestions.reason: The desired behavior described in the eval note offers two acceptable shapes — 'no file yet (questions are the deliverable)' OR 'a file with unfilled sections explicitly pending.' The executor chose to create a fully-templated file with placeholders AND ask. Both the no-fabrication and ask-the-user goals were met, but expectation 5's disjunction means a borderline run that drafts a file but omits one required section (e.g., no Plano de entrega heading at all) could still arguably 'pass' under the first disjunct ('no file yet') reasoning. Consider tightening to: 'If a file is produced, every required section heading is present and any unsubstantiated section is explicitly marked pending.'

suggestions.assertion: Does not fabricate risks, delivery phases, or cons the user never stated
suggestions.reason: This is the most discriminating assertion and it held well. To make it even harder to game, consider adding a positive check that the ✓ benefit lines trace only to given facts (recall recovery / reuse of pgvector) and contain no invented metrics — a weaker skill might invent a latency number or a percentage target, which this run correctly avoided ('Se quiser um alvo explícito ... me diz o X').

eval_feedback.overall: Evals are solid and discriminating; this run is a clean pass on all five. The skill genuinely asked for the missing Compensações/Riscos/Plano substance in Portuguese, stayed faithful to the four given facts, and avoided fabricating any cons, risks, or delivery phases while keeping every required template section present-but-pending.
